rationale: Across the published discovery cohort and clinical registry evaluations of KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621390), 14 individuals with de novo missense variants were identified: 11 harboring the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant and 3 harboring non-recurrent missense variants. All variants cluster within the Kelch-type beta-propeller substrate-binding domain. Clinical manifestations, specifically the presence and spectrum of seizures (ranging from febrile seizures to epilepsy/infantile spasms), display phenotypic overlap across both recurrent and non-recurrent Kelch domain variant carriers without documented significant divergence in penetrance, semiology, or age of onset.

evidence.text: Fourteen patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20 delineate a neurodevelopmental syndrome characterized by intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphisms. Eleven patients harbor the recurrent c.1069G>A p.(Gly357Arg) variant, and three carry private missense variants, all clustering in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein, which shapes the substrate binding surface.

new_directions.question_text: Do electroclinical seizure characteristics and antiepileptic drug responsiveness differ quantitatively in an expanded cohort of non-recurrent Kelch-domain missense carriers versus p.Gly357Arg carriers?
new_directions.rationale: The initial discovery cohort only contained 3 individuals with non-recurrent variants compared to 11 with p.Gly357Arg, limiting statistical power to identify subtle variations in seizure onset timing, refractoriness, or specific semiologies.

new_directions.question_text: How do non-Kelch domain variants or putative loss-of-function variants in KLHL20 impact seizure penetrance relative to beta-propeller missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: All currently characterized individuals have missense variants localized to the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain; determining whether haploinsufficiency or variants outside the Kelch domain phenocopy the seizure phenotype is critical to clarify disease mechanisms.
